new.title: Meet Boze Griet at Bastion Oranje
new.desc: Bastion Oranje was added to the city walls in 1634 and still holds back the water today. Inside the half-buried Bastionder visitor centre a short film tells how the 'swamp dragon' city was defended, and the restored cannon Boze Griet (Angry Greta) stands guard.
new.tip: The fortress boat tour moors here between April and October, so you can combine the bastion with a trip along the walls by water.

new.title: Explore the old De Gruyter factory
new.desc: De Gruyter was once the biggest employer in town, with hundreds of shops selling only its own coffee, jam and biscuits made in this factory on the Veemarktkade. Restored in 2010, the building is now a buzzing hub for some 200 creative businesses.
new.tip: Volunteer guides of Kring Vrienden van 's-Hertogenbosch run tours full of stories from former employees; ask about the famous 'candy of the week' for children.

new.title: Watch the Binnendieze flow under Uilenburg
new.desc: Uilenburg is one of the oldest corners of the city, a tight little quarter where the Binnendieze slips between and under the houses. Once run down, it is now full of narrow alleys, eetcafes and terraces right by the water.
new.tip: Stand on the little bridge and look for the boats of the Binnendieze tour disappearing under the buildings; it is the best free view of the hidden river.

new.title: Get into the Oeteldonk spirit at the carnival museum
new.desc: The Oeteldonks Gemintemuzejum, run by enthusiastic volunteers, fills a medieval convent gateway by the Binnendieze with carnival masks, costumes, posters, shields and even a three-metre Peruvian hat.
new.tip: Visit outside carnival season to understand the frog symbols, the Knillis legend and the colours you will see all over town in February.

new.title: See Brabant's Van Goghs at Het Noordbrabants Museum
new.desc: Behind the stately 18th-century facade of the former governor's residence hangs the art of the province, including paintings from Van Gogh's Nuenen period, works from the school of Jheronimus Bosch and Brueghel etchings.
new.tip: A corridor links it to the Design Museum next door, so one afternoon covers both; the museum garden behind is a calm spot for a break.

new.title: Rethink everyday objects at the Design Museum
new.desc: Design Museum Den Bosch looks at what design means for society, from ceramics and jewellery to bold exhibitions such as its widely discussed show on design in the Third Reich.
new.tip: Check what is on before you go: the temporary exhibitions are the main draw and change several times a year.
new.q: Design Museum Den Bosch De Mortel 4

new.title: Spot the oldest brick house on the Markt
new.desc: De Moriaan, with its stepped gable on the corner of the Markt, dates from the 13th century and is said to be the oldest brick building in the Netherlands. It now houses the tourist office.
new.tip: Slip behind the building to its quiet courtyard for a coffee away from the market bustle.

new.title: Look up at the swan on the Zwanenbroedershuis
new.desc: The Illustre Lieve Vrouwe Broederschap, a religious brotherhood founded in 1318, has met in this house on the Hinthamerstraat since 1484. A swan crowns the gable, and inside a small museum shows choir books, altarpieces and centuries of brotherhood treasures.
new.tip: The house is only open at set times or with a guide from Kring Vrienden, so check ahead; the facade alone is worth a stop on the way to the Sint-Jan.

new.title: Walk the star-shaped Citadel
new.desc: The Citadel, nicknamed Papenbril, is a star-shaped fortress built between 1637 and 1642 on the north side of the city. Today it holds the provincial archives, and the green ramparts around it make a peaceful loop.
new.tip: Across the water stands the hexagonal Kruithuis, the old gunpowder store; walk between the two for the best sense of the old defences.

new.title: Find the brewery above the curiosity shop
new.desc: Brouwerij Boegbeeld brews its beer on the floor above La Folie, an antique and curiosity shop on Uilenburg, in an 1836 building that once stored liqueur and wine.
new.tip: Go up the stairs at the back of the shop; you can buy bottles when the shop is open and the brewer is in.

new.title: Drink a Kraanwater at Bossche Brouwers on the Tramkade
new.desc: The silos and halls of the old De Heus feed mill on the Tramkade have become one of the city's most creative hangouts. Bossche Brouwers started with a beer kit from HEMA and now pours its own brews in a taproom with a terrace and live music.
new.tip: Find it behind the Mengfabriek through the passage to the Werkwarenhuis; try the blonde Kraanwater, named after the crane hotel next door.
new.q: Bossche Brouwers aan de Vaart Tramkade 's-Hertogenbosch

new.title: Eat among the locals at Eten bij Fret
new.desc: This simple, friendly restaurant on the Postelstraat is a budget favourite where you really feel you are sitting with the people of Den Bosch rather than with other tourists.
new.tip: Come early in the evening; it is small and fills up quickly with regulars.

new.title: Grab a warm worstenbroodje at the Markt
new.desc: On market days the triangular Markt fills with stalls of cheese, bread and Brabant specialities. Look for the Keilekker stand selling the Brabantsche worstenbroodje, a soft bread roll wrapped around spiced minced meat.
new.tip: The big markets are on Wednesday and Saturday; eat your worstenbroodje warm, standing next to the Jheronimus Bosch statue.

new.title: Walk into the marsh that defended the city
new.desc: The Bossche Broek starts right behind the station and the old walls. This wet grassland once made the city the 'invincible swamp dragon' until Frederik Hendrik drained it to win the siege of 1629; now it is a nature reserve full of meadow birds and orchids.
new.tip: Walk out from the Zuidwal for the classic view back at the Sint-Jan rising over the fields, best in the evening light.

new.title: Ride the glass lift up the Jheronimus Bosch Art Center
new.desc: A former church on the Jeroen Boschplein shows full-size replicas of all of Bosch's paintings plus 3D versions of his strange creatures. A glass lift in the tower then takes you about 40 metres up for a view over the city.
new.tip: Don't skip the old boiler room downstairs, where Bosch's studio has been recreated.
new.q: Jheronimus Bosch Art Center Jeroen Boschplein 2 's-Hertogenbosch

new.title: Hunt for the hidden Tilmanshofje
new.desc: Tucked behind the Parklaan in the old working-class quarter of Vughtereinde, the Tilmanshofje is a little courtyard of houses where the staff of a wealthy family once lived. Nearby alleys like Achter de Kan carry names that tell old stories.
new.tip: Kring Vrienden van 's-Hertogenbosch runs an alleyway walk from the Kruisbroedershof that passes it; on your own, walk quietly, people live here.

new.title: Hear a Sunday concert in the Kruithuis courtyard
new.desc: The hexagonal Kruithuis, a former gunpowder arsenal opposite the Citadel, is now a museum. In summer its historic courtyard turns into an intimate stage for Sunday morning chamber concerts.
new.tip: Book through the museum and pair the concert with coffee and a Bossche bol in the courtyard.

new.title: Reflect at Nationaal Monument Kamp Vught
new.desc: During the Second World War the Germans ran a concentration camp in Vught. The memorial on part of the former camp has a rebuilt barrack and watchtowers, the original crematorium and the Monument of the Lost Children.
new.tip: Allow at least two hours. It is a short bike ride from Den Bosch, or take the train to Vught and walk about 20 minutes.
new.q: Nationaal Monument Kamp Vught Lunettenlaan 600 Vught

new.title: Visit the collector's castle of Heeswijk
new.desc: Kasteel Heeswijk on the river Aa goes back to around 1080 and once hosted Louis XIV. In the 19th century the Van den Bogaerde family restored it in neo-Gothic style and filled it with paintings, armour and curiosities, the story the museum tells today.
new.tip: Combine it with the Abdij van Berne, a short walk or bike ride away in the same village.

new.title: Step back in time in tiny Megen on the Maas
new.desc: Megen in the Maaskant is a tiny Maas town with a medieval street plan, the 14th-century Gevangenpoort (prison gate), a Franciscan friary, a Poor Clares convent and the windmill Desire.
new.tip: Cycle here from Oss or along the Maas dike; the Gevangenpoort and the mill are a few minutes apart, so the whole town fits in an easy stroll.

new.title: Admire Kasteel Nieuw-Herlaer from the Dommel
new.desc: This castle on the Dommel near Sint-Michielsgestel was first mentioned in 1381; its 15th-century octagonal stair tower survives next to a house rebuilt in 1791. It later served as a seminary and an institute for the deaf.
new.tip: The castle is privately owned, so enjoy it from the bridge at the hamlet of Halder or from the walking paths along the Dommel.

new.title: Taste Berne abbey beer in Heeswijk
new.desc: The Abdij van Berne, founded in 1134, is the oldest still active monastic community in the Netherlands. Since 2015 volunteers have revived its abbey beer, and the profits help maintain the buildings.
new.tip: Join a guided tour of the abbey grounds and finish in the proeflokaal (tasting room); the abbey shop sells the beers and regional products.

new.title: Hunt down Brabant's best worstenbroodje in Vught
new.desc: The Brabantsche Worstenbroodjes bakery at Fort Isabella in Vught bakes a worstenbroodje that food writers rate among the tastiest in the province: golden bread around a juicy, well-seasoned sausage.
new.tip: Buy a bag and eat them warm on a walk around the nearby IJzeren Man lake.

new.title: Taste camel milk in Berlicum
new.desc: Kamelenmelkerij Smits in Berlicum, just east of Den Bosch, is often called the only camel dairy in Europe. A herd of camels grazes in the Brabant meadows and their milk ends up in the farm shop.
new.tip: Try something made with the milk and say hello to the camels; the farm also runs group visits, so check ahead if you want a tour.

new.title: Have a drink at Honderd Bunder Bos by the dunes
new.desc: On the sheltered north edge of the Loonse en Drunense Duinen near Drunen, the terrace of Honderd Bunder Bos (with a mini golf course) is a classic stop before or after a walk into the drifting sand.
new.tip: From here it is a short walk south through the forest to the open sand plain.

new.title: Cross the Moerputten bridge over the marsh
new.desc: This 585-metre iron railway bridge on 35 brick pillars once carried the 'Halve Zolenlijntje', the train of the shoe-making Langstraat. Restored in 2011, it now lets walkers cross the peat ponds and reed beds of the Moerputten.
new.tip: The bridge is for walkers only; follow the Halve Zolenpad from the Vlijmen side for a loop through the marsh.

new.title: Take the bike ferry from little Ravenstein
new.desc: Ravenstein on the Maas was long a Catholic enclave outside the Dutch Republic, a refuge for monks and churchgoers. Two early 16th-century round bastions, rediscovered in the dike in 1997, still carry cannons that the local guild fires a few times a year.
new.tip: Between April and October a bicycle ferry crosses the Maas to Niftrik; the tourist information point in the old town hall has route maps.

new.title: Look for wisent in De Maashorst
new.desc: De Maashorst is a big landscape park of heath, forest and sand between Oss and Uden. Since 2016 European bison (wisent) and Exmoor ponies roam part of it freely.
new.tip: Start at the visitor centre in Slabroek near Nistelrode, where most walking routes begin, and keep a respectful distance from the animals.

new.title: Climb the Onverflout watchtower at Den Dungen
new.desc: In 1629 3,000 soldiers camped on the Keerdijk at Den Dungen to attack the city. The art watchtower Onverflout ('always stay brave') marks the spot, with lines from a 17th-century song book on its walls.
new.tip: Walk the 3.5 km Zuiderwaterlinie route from the chapel at the corner of Keerdijk and Bosscheweg, where a model shows the old army camp.

new.title: Roll down the drifting sand in Rosmalen
new.desc: The Rosmalense Zandverstuiving is a small patch of woods and drifting sand on the edge of Rosmalen, dotted with artworks by Armando and Wiel van Rosmalen.
new.tip: Enter from the Deken van Roestellaan or the Oude Baan; it is a good short outing with children, who love rolling down the sand.
